title: Pudgy Penguins sets key deadlines ahead of major shutdown
detail:
Pudgy Penguins sets key deadlines ahead of major shutdown
Anand Sinha
Mon, November 23, 2026 at 6:30 PM MST 3 min read
PENGU34466-USD
WMT
Trade PENGU on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Pudgy Penguins, the plush toy brand that has become a fixture in Walmart stores across the U.S., last week announced a key deadline as another project from its parent company nears shutdown.

The brand started out in 2021 as a collection of non-fungible tokens (NFTs). It became so popular that it branched out into soft toys, which turned into a hit of their own.

Related: What is an NFT? It could be the future of live events

In simple words, an NFT is a digital certificate of ownership existing on a blockchain network that proves you own a particular, unique digital artwork.

Anyone can buy a replica of Klimt's "The Kiss" but the real ownership belongs to the holder who has the certificate proving the original's authenticity.

It is especially crucial in the digital world where replicas are very common. Anyone can download a picture of a penguin. The NFT is the record proving you own the original, stored on a blockchain.

More on TheStreet Roundtable:

Ripple CEO sees crypto rebound, draws Anthropic IPO-SpaceX parallel

Six senators push Treasury to protect state-regulated stablecoin issuers

Analyst sounds alarm over New York pension fund's major investment

Pudgy Penguins parent announced Abstract shutdown last month

As the NFT market peaked in 2021 and crashed soon after, most penguin or dog-based collections lost value. But Pudgy Penguins decided to launch as plushies in physical stores.

In September 2023, it partnered with Walmart to launch Pudgy Toys — plushies, figurines, games, and collectibles — in 2,000 U.S. stores and on Walmart's website. The toys became extremely popular among customers at the retail giant.

In January 2025, Pudgy Penguins' parent company, Igloo Inc., decided the time was ripe to return to its crypto roots and launched its own blockchain network, Abstract.

The goal was to turn those retail customers into an online community built around games, apps and digital collectibles existing within a crypto ecosystem.

But Igloo last month announced the blockchain project is shutting down on Dec. 15 because there are not enough takers for it.

Pudgy Penguins shares 2 deadlines for SBT holders

On Nov. 19, Pudgy Penguins opened the migration tool to let holders move their Soulbound tokens (SBTs) off the Abstract network.

An SBT is just an NFT but there is a catch: it is permanently tied to a wallet and cannot be transferred or sold.

Anyone holding SBTs on Abstract has until Dec. 15 to move them to another network, Pudgy Penguins said.

The company also announced that holders of the Box Burnooor SBTs — an NFT collection by Pudgy Penguins — can claim a free Vibes TCG "Table for Two" Booster Box. Vibes is a physical/digital trading card game that features Pudgy Penguins.

title: Is Amazon's Profit Riskier Than It Looks?
detail:
Is Amazon's Profit Riskier Than It Looks?
Trefis Team
Mon, November 23, 2026 at 5:25 PM MST 5 min read
ANT
AMZN
NVDA
^NDX
GOOG
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Today's big story: Reported SEC Probe: Could Nvidia Stock Fall To $92?

Update, Nov 23: Large tech stocks rose in Monday morning trading after Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. Amazon rose about 4%, to about $256, and the Nasdaq 100 fund (QQQ) rose about 7%, while Anthropic was about flat. The figures below are at Friday's close.

Amazon.com (AMZN) closed at $246.82 on Friday, Nov 20. That was a fall of 4.1% for the day. Anthropic (ANT), newly listed, fell 8.5% on its second day of trading. Why mention both? This article looks at how much of Amazon's profit came from gains on stocks and stakes it holds, and what a slide like Anthropic's could mean for that profit.

The answer is a large share. Over the four quarters to September 2026, 40.1% of Amazon's pre-tax income was non-operating income. That is profit from outside the business itself, such as gains on stocks and stakes a company owns. Almost all of it was gains on securities, $69.7 billion.

That is new for Amazon. From 2019 to 2022, non-operating items were a small net loss, -6.0% of pre-tax income. From 2023 to September 2025, they were 9.3% of pre-tax income. So Amazon's reported profit now rises and falls with the prices of what it holds. The income statements do not show which holdings produced the gains. So we do not size any single one, Anthropic included.

Which Quarter Brought In Most Of The Gains?

Most of it came in one quarter. In the three months to June 2026, Amazon's non-operating income was $53.4 billion. That was 66.0% of its pre-tax income. It was also the largest of any quarter since the start of 2019.

Net income that quarter was $62.6 billion. Operating income, the profit from selling goods and services, was $27.5 billion. So net income was 2.3 times operating income.

Amazon's net income in the three months to June was 2.3 times its operating income. If Amazon is a big part of your savings, the profit it reports can drop fast when the stocks it holds fall. When the market has fallen, the Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio has lost about 81 cents for every $1 its benchmark lost, on average. See the HQ record.

Net income also ran 1.4 times operating cash flow that quarter. Operating cash flow is the cash the business brings in from customers after its running costs.

Did The Gains Keep Coming After June?

No. In the three months to September, Amazon had a non-operating loss of $1.2 billion. Gains on securities became a loss of $0.7 billion. Operating income that quarter was $28.1 billion.

Nvidia Adds Nearly $1 Trillion in Value as Trump Hails Huang as a "National Treasure." It's Still Cheaper Than Walmart ©Nana Dua from Pexels and Karola G from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

NVIDIA shares jumped 31% today after its board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, adding nearly $1 trillion of market value.

The November selloff priced in a leadership crisis while analysts kept raising NVIDIA's earnings estimates.

Even after the jump, NVIDIA trades at a forward P/E in the low teens, against 41x for Walmart.

Cisco fell 79% after a 24% day in 2001, so the open investigation and reported SEC probe still matter, and Dell's Nov. 24 results are the next test.

NVIDIA (NVDA:NASDAQ) just had the biggest day any stock has ever had.

Its board reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director before today's open. He had resigned 11 days earlier, amid reports that he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The stock jumped 31% and added nearly $1 trillion of market value in the first two hours of trading. If that holds, it's far bigger than the $450 billion one-day record Microsoft (MSFT:NASDAQ) set.

President Trump weighed in on Truth Social: "On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure."

And yet NVIDIA is still far cheaper than Walmart (WMT:NASDAQ) on forward earnings.

Dell Technologies (DELL:NYSE) builds AI servers around NVIDIA's chips, and it jumped 20% ahead of its own results on Nov. 24. The bears already point to Cisco (CSCO:NASDAQ) and its 2001 crash.

The selloff never touched the earnings

NVIDIA fell 38% in November through Friday. The month brought AI-skeptical midterm results, Huang's resignation and a lukewarm reception for Anthropic's record IPO. Analysts kept raising their numbers the whole time. Consensus has normalized EPS of $9.67 for fiscal 2027, which ends in January, more than double fiscal 2026's $4.77. For fiscal 2028 the figure is $16.61, up another 72%, and a month ago it was $15.92:

Nvidia (NVDA): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024-2028 (years to January) (TIKR)

Management guided in August for fiscal 2028 revenue to grow about 70%, and said supply was what limited that figure.

So the price did all the falling. NVIDIA's forward P/E hit 10x on Nov. 19, its lowest in five years. Its five-year average is 36x, and it peaked at 70x in May 2023:

Nvidia (NVDA): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

Today's jump only lifts it to the low teens. That's a steep discount for an 11-day absence: NYU Stern professor Aswath Damodaran put a short-lived CEO disruption at 3% to 5% of NVIDIA's value.

Target Has "Out-Comped Walmart Three Quarters in a Row." Walmart Still Trades at More Than 2x Its Multiple ©Nodar Chernishev from Getty Images and Tatarinov Andrey from Изображения пользователя Андрей via Canva
Key Takeaways

Target's comparable sales rose 5.6% last quarter on 5.0% more traffic, while Walmart's U.S. comps rose 2.9% and its in-store sales fell again.

Walmart still trades at 41x forward earnings, more than twice Target's 17x, while Costco trades at 48x and Kroger at 13x.

Walmart's premium rests on e-commerce, advertising and membership, but its operating margin has stayed between 4.0% and 4.5% for five years.

At 17x, Target looks like the better buy, and Walmart's February outlook has to show profit growing well ahead of sales.

Target (TGT:NYSE) just did something that should bother Walmart (WMT:NASDAQ) shareholders, at least a little.

Target's comparable sales rose 5.6% in the third quarter it reported Wednesday, on a 5.0% jump in traffic. Walmart followed on Thursday with U.S. comps of 2.9%, and its in-store comparable sales fell again.

As Stephanie Link, chief investment strategist at Hightower Advisors, put it on Friday's episode of CNBC's Halftime Report:

"They have now out-comped Walmart three quarters in a row."

And yet Walmart trades at 41x forward earnings, against 17x for Target. Of its big rivals, only Costco (COST:NASDAQ) costs more, at 48x, while Kroger (KR:NYSE) trades at just 13x.

That's a whole lot of premium for the retailer losing the comps race.

Walmart's growth is coming from outside the store

Walmart's revenue rose 5% to $188.8 billion, with its fastest growth outside the store aisles: global e-commerce grew 17%, U.S. advertising 37% and membership fee revenue 17%.

Analysts expect that mix to lift earnings about 11% a year, from fiscal 2026's $2.64 a share to $3.61 in fiscal 2029:

Walmart (WMT): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024-2028 (years to January) (TIKR)

Walmart raised this fiscal year's guidance to $2.84-$2.89, topping out at the $2.89 analysts already expect.

TIKR tracks 39 analysts on Target. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Target, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Target's Analyst Ratings

Target's lead comes off a smaller, softer base

Walmart's quarterly revenue was nearly 7x Target's $27.1 billion, so its 2.9% adds far more dollars than Target's 5.6%. Target is also lapping a rough year: it credits part of its gross margin gain to last year's elevated markdowns, and its $2.65 of adjusted EPS includes $0.50 of tariff refunds.

Still, the turnaround looks real. Excluding the refunds, adjusted EPS rose 21%, and Target's traffic gain beat Walmart's 1.5% transaction growth.

Key Takeaways

Of the 460 big funds that have filed 13Fs for the quarter ended Sept. 30, 12 bought KLA and 12 sold it. Ken Fisher's firm added 63% to its stake, and Brad Gerstner's Altimeter Capital sold all of its shares.

Altimeter also sold all of its Applied Materials and Lam Research, while KLA's biggest buyer, GQG Partners, opened a much larger new stake in Lam.

KLA is down 35% since Sept. 30 and trades at about 20x forward earnings, below its 25x five-year average, with earnings per share expected to rise 53% in the fiscal year to June 2027.

Five of the buyers sold or cut Walmart, which is up 23% since Sept. 30, so the sellers look right so far, but at today's price the buyers look like the better bet.

Big funds couldn't agree on KLA (KLAC:NASDAQ) last quarter, and the stock has fallen 35% since.

Of the 460 big funds that have filed 13Fs for the quarter ended Sept. 30, 12 bought KLA and 12 sold it, while 31 held it at the quarter's end. The counts include funds readers know by name and any fund with $1 billion or more of US stocks in its 13F, leaving out quant and index funds. A buy is a new position or 20% or more shares added, and a sale is selling out or cutting 20% or more.

Altimeter sold out, and GQG made the biggest buy

Brad Gerstner's Altimeter Capital sold all 578,230 of its KLA shares, about $174 million at quarter-end prices, according to its 13F for the quarter ended Sept. 30, filed Nov. 16. The stake had been 1.8% of its 13F stocks a quarter earlier, and the firm manages $19 billion in all. Parnassus Investments, a $41 billion firm, sold nearly as much, about $172 million, in its 13F filed Oct. 22. Its 20% cut still left it 3.52 million shares worth $687 million, its 16th-largest holding.

On the other side, GQG Partners, a $164 billion firm, opened an 863,882-share position worth about $168 million, 0.3% of its 13F stocks, in its filing of Nov. 13. Ken Fisher's Fisher Investments, which manages $387 billion, raised its stake 63%, to 533,311 shares, in its 13F filed Nov. 6. At $104 million, that's still less than 0.1% of its 13F stocks.

title: Can Walmart Sustain Its Q3 Sales Momentum Through the Holiday Season?
detail:
Can Walmart Sustain Its Q3 Sales Momentum Through the Holiday Season?
Vrishali Bagree
Mon, November 23, 2026 at 8:15 AM MST 3 min read
WMT
TGT
COST
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Walmart Inc. WMT is entering the holiday shopping season with encouraging sales momentum, supported by grocery market share gains, e-commerce demand and competitive pricing. Third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues increased 5.2% year over year to $188.8 billion, or 4.5% in constant currency, as the retailer continued attracting shoppers across income groups.

Walmart U.S. comparable sales, excluding fuel, rose 2.9%, improving from 2.6% in the preceding quarter. Transactions increased 1.5%, while the average ticket grew 1.4%. Grocery sales advanced at a mid-single-digit rate, while general merchandise sales grew at a low-single-digit pace. Grocery market share gains were among the strongest in three years.

Convenience remained another demand driver. Walmart U.S. e-commerce sales climbed 23%, marking the eleventh consecutive quarter of growth exceeding 20%. Store-fulfilled deliveries increased more than 40%, reflecting continued demand for convenient shopping options.

Early holiday trends have been encouraging. Walmart maintained approximately 7,700 price rollbacks in the United States at quarter-end. Its 26-item Thanksgiving meal offering included comparable items priced about 12% below last year's levels. Walmart had also sold one million more turkeys than at the same point last year.

For the fourth quarter, Walmart expects enterprise sales growth of 4.5% to 5.5% in constant currency, aided by an approximately one-percentage-point benefit from Flipkart's Big Billion Days timing shift. U.S. comparable sales growth is expected to remain similar to the third quarter. While grocery strength, competitive pricing and faster delivery support holiday demand, some early purchases may reflect spending pulled forward. Sustaining sales momentum will depend on whether shoppers maintain their spending pace throughout the holiday season.

How Are COST & TGT Positioned for Holiday Sales?

Costco Wholesale Corporation COST is entering the holiday season with strong sales momentum. COST's October 2026 net sales increased 12.6% year over year to $24.5 billion, while comparable sales rose 11.1%. Excluding gasoline-price and foreign-exchange impacts, comparable sales grew 7.3%. Digitally enabled sales climbed 22.5%, reflecting sustained online demand. Costco's value-focused offerings and consistent sales growth provide a solid foundation for maintaining customer spending through the holiday shopping season.

Target Corporation TGT is approaching the holiday season with improving sales momentum. The company's third-quarter 2026 net sales increased 7.1%, while comparable sales grew 5.6%, driven by 5% traffic growth. TGT's digital comparable sales advanced 9.8%. November sales trends accelerated from October, remaining in line with expectations. Target is attracting holiday shoppers with more than 8,000 new gifts, including thousands priced at $5 and under, alongside promotional deals and a $30 Thanksgiving meal for six.
